title: Provenance-weighted reconciliation + freshness badging to fix per-model attribution noise from late/duplicate meter events
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Console per-model breakdowns and tenant heatmaps show recurring micro-spikes and attribution 'smear' after late ingest/backfills and retry fan-in from rate-limit retries. Current mitigation (dedupe by event id + last-writer heuristics) reduces obvious duplicates but fails when small deltas (sequence offsets, partial KV cache prefixes) create near-duplicate events that should be partially attributed across model aliases. This causes noisy charts, incorrect hourly cost signals, and occasional small billing disputes for high-volume tenants.

Goal: Implement a provenance-weighted reconciliation pipeline that assigns probabilistic provenance scores to events at ingest time, supports retroactive reweighting during deterministic backfills, and exposes data-freshness indicators in the Console to make per-model attribution auditable and visibly correctable. The approach should preserve deterministic billing under current SLA while improving analytics fidelity and UX.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Event provenance vector: augment ingested usage events with a flat metadata string vector (source, shard-id, ingest-time, retry-count, trace-id-hash, dedupe-candidate-score). This is stored as part of the ledger row (compact, opaque).
2) Probabilistic attribution: during aggregation, compute a provenance score for each event versus candidate model identities; when provenance is ambiguous, split token attribution proportionally rather than forcing single-model assignment. This avoids permanent mis-attribution caused by late small offsets.
3) Backfill reconciliation job: a scheduled deterministically-ordered reprocessor that replays backfills and late events, recalculates provenance weights, and emits compact delta corrections to the aggregation layer. Corrections are applied as idempotent adjustments rather than row deletions to preserve audit trails.
4) Freshness badging in Console: show per-chart indicators (stale/partial/final) with a provenance-confidence metric and a tooltip explaining if the data is provisional due to pending backfills. Provide an 'apply pending corrections' toggle for workspace admins to preview reconciled charts.
5) Billing conservatism: for billing-facing aggregates (charges, credits), default to conservative rounding rules during provisional windows; only finalize billing invoices after reconciliation window completes or when admin triggers finalization.

Technical notes/specs:
- Storage: ledger rows remain immutable; append 'correction' rows referencing original IDs. Corrections are compact string-encoded deltas.
- Determinism: reconciliation job must be idempotent and deterministic across regions; use stable sort keys (tenant, model_alias, event_epoch) and a provenance-hash seed.
- Performance: attribution splitting happens in the aggregation tier; implement fast path for clear single-provenance events to avoid added latency. Add sampling-mode to reconciliation for large tenants to bound cost.
- Telemetry: emit trial metrics (provenance_confidence_distribution, corrected_token_delta, provisional_fraction_by_model) and dashboards to evaluate impact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Aggregation pipeline produces <= 2% reduction in per-model high-frequency noise (measured by 5-min spike count) on a synthetic tenant replay test set.
- Console shows freshness badge and the confidence score for every per-model chart within the UI.
- Backfill reconciliation job completes for 30 days of history for a staging tenant within SLA (24h for 30d) and produces idempotent corrections.
- No change in finalized billing invoices for past finalized periods; provisional windows default to conservative billing semantics and are documented in UI tooltip.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): implement provenance vector schema and aggregation split logic behind feature flag; run synthetic tenant replays; validate metrics and performance (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (canary tenants): enable reconciliation for 3 low-risk customers and surface freshness badges; solicit CS/AE feedback (1 week).
- Phase 3 (wide): enable by default for all console tenants, keep conservative billing finalization for 72h window after backfill; monitor for anomalies (2 weeks).

Monitoring & alerting:
- New SLOs: reconciliation-lag (median, p95), applied-correction-rate, provisional-chart-fraction; set alerts if correction-rate > 0.5% sustained for high-volume tenants.
- Postdeploy checks: reconcile applied corrections for 7-day window and validate no >0.1% divergence in total token counts compared to prior canonical ledger scan.

- Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/provenance-recon-staging

comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Identified as high-impact for billing disputes; prioritized P1. Owner assigned Marco Liu.
2026-03-03 - Architecture sync: Agreed on append-only correction rows and idempotent reconciliation. Decided to keep ledger immutability (no physical deletes).
2026-03-05 - Design review: UX recommended three badge states (final, provisional, partial) plus tooltip copy. PM requested conservative billing default during provisional window.
2026-03-07 - Prototype: Ingest team pushed schema change branch and added provenance fields; unit tests for lightweight scoring added. PR 4721 opened for initial review.
2026-03-09 - Load test: Synthetic tenant replay (1M events) shows 8% extra CPU in aggregation for full-split path; agreed to optimize fast-path and add tenant-sampling for reconciliation.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: Finalize provenance scoring algorithm, add telemetry metrics, and schedule staging rollout. QA test cases for billing conservatism in progress.
